facts.value: While animation frames remain, this callback performs no cleanup or recovery transition. Once they expire, it clears Kirby's stored arrow and bow references without directly destroying either item. For a Link or CLINK copy, it selects the corresponding freefall attribute: zero calls ftCo_Fall_Enter; nonzero calls ftCo_80096900 with that value as landing_lag. The latter routine normally enters FallSpecial but has a separate x2224_b2 branch; its eventual special-landing transition is also conditional.
facts.rationale: Corrects direct article-removal wording and preserves the recovery parameter's actual consumer and exceptional branches.

evidence.why: Unset helpers only clear fighter references.
Animation guard and copy-specific recovery selection.
Landing-lag storage and exceptional entry branch.

facts.value: This empty callback performs no input test, timer update, charge change or motion-state transition. Other callbacks own aerial End progression: physics delegates to common airborne movement, collision handles pending release and ground continuity, and animation completion clears the fighter's arrow and bow references before selecting ordinary fall or configured fall-special recovery. Reference clearing is not direct item destruction.
facts.rationale: Preserves the supported no-op role while correcting the companion animation's article-lifetime description.

facts.value: During grounded copied-bow Start, this callback unconditionally delegates to ft_80084F3C and has no local timer or action-state transition. The helper starts with common ground friction and multiplies it by friction_when_above_walk_speed when absolute ground velocity exceeds maximum walking velocity, then applies friction and ground movement. The source establishes scaled friction, not that the scale necessarily increases it.
facts.rationale: Removes the unsupported claim that the runtime multiplier necessarily produces stronger friction.

evidence.why: Runtime scaling without a specified multiplier value.

facts.rationale: Unlike IsDrawback, this semantic name exposes bow construction and the unusual true-for-abort convention. It is a descriptive hypothesis, not a recovered original name.

evidence.why: Creates a bow only for an empty slot; true means occupied slot or creation failure.
Both entry routines interpret true as an abort.

facts.rationale: Describes the actual tracked-bow removal operation instead of borrowing Link's fighter-variable offset terminology; parallels the supported DestroyArrow name.

evidence.why: Paired arrow and bow removal helpers.
Bow helper forwards to generic item removal.

facts.value: When x78 is empty, the helper attempts to create the copy-specific bow at R3rdNa. Success stores the bow, reinstalls copied-special callbacks and returns false. An already occupied x78 or failed constructor returns true. Both entry callers treat true as an abort and clear their arrow and bow references, without directly removing those articles. Ground entry invokes common action completion; air entry selects ordinary fall for a zero copy-specific recovery value or calls configured fall-special recovery otherwise.
facts.rationale: Corrects article-removal wording without losing the occupied-slot abort or distinct ground/air recovery paths.

facts.value: Grounded activation clears the charge and enable components, timer and four command variables, performs common grounded setup and zeroes vertical self-velocity. It selects Link or CLINK grounded Start at frame zero and base rate one, then applies the copy-specific charge animation rate and initializes animation processing. Startup continues only when bow setup returns false. A true result, including an already occupied bow slot, clears the fighter's arrow and bow references and invokes ft_8008A2BC for common action completion; it does not directly destroy those items or guarantee an unconditional Wait transition.
facts.rationale: Replaces immediate article-removal wording and preserves the common completion dispatcher's exceptional branches.
